A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cybench study and provide comparable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The reduction from 151 to 150 pages reflects reflow, not missing experimental or appendix material.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of language-model agents on 40 CTF tasks, including model and scaffold comparisons in Tables 2–3 and detailed appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original model evaluations, scaffold comparisons, supplementary experiments, and detailed task-level results.

M1.justification: The act–execute–update procedure, memory handling, response fields, subtask mechanism, and four agent scaffolds are unchanged in Sections 2–4 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 40 tasks from HackTheBox, SekaiCTF, Glacier, and HKCert across six categories. Removing the introductory footnote about additional task contributions does not change the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 compares the same eight models. Table 3 retains structured bash, action-only, pseudoterminal, and web-search comparisons for Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o; appendix comparator membership also matches.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the 15-iteration unguided limit, five iterations per subtask, and identical token limits, including the o1-preview exception. Evaluation metrics and appendix settings, including the full-history experiment, are unchanged.

E4.justification: The scaffold analyses, subtask-submission analysis, FST-weighted evaluation, full-history experiment in Table 9, and appendix refusal analyses and examples are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both report single-attempt model evaluations and maximum performance over three attempts for scaffold comparisons. Run-count disclosures, aggregation practices, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix result entries match. For example, Table 2 retains 17.5% unguided performance for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, 12.5% for GPT-4o, and 46.8% subtask performance for o1-preview. Figure findings and detailed task results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The act–execute–update equations in Section 2.5 and formal environment definitions in Appendix G are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, eight-item contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about the benchmark, subtasks, difficulty coverage, and agent evaluations. The deleted footnote does not alter these core contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of first solve time, scaffold complexity, and train–test overlap are unchanged. Appendix I retains the same qualifications concerning limited scaffolding, reasoning capabilities, and the realism and scale of CTF tasks.

D1.justification: Prompts, model identifiers, environment setup, task-verification procedures, token budgets, and code/data availability information are unchanged. The PDFs also retain identical external link targets.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning against InterCode-CTF, the NYU CTF Dataset, and prior cybersecurity agents in Section 6.

P1.justification: v4 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header and deletes Section 1's footnote stating that additional CTF task contributions had been received. Remaining prose and section organization are unchanged, with subsequent footnotes renumbered.

P2.justification: Spacing and pagination change in the main text, allowing the conclusion to finish on page 10 instead of continuing onto page 11. Later material shifts forward one page. Figures, table structures, and captions retain their content.

improvement.justification: v4 mainly updates publication formatting, tightens pagination, and removes an ancillary footnote. The methods, evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These modest presentation edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
